title: Nuclear Incident
description: Use this list to prepare for a nuclear detonation or fallout emergency - the core actions are Get Inside, Stay Inside, Stay Tuned.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions on Potassium Iodide (KI)

items.text: If you see a bright flash, look away, drop face down behind something solid, and cover your head - stay down until the shock waves pass
Know the best shelter near home and work: the basement or center of a brick or concrete building, away from outside walls and roof - a car is poor shelter
Plan to stay inside at least 24 hours unless officials say otherwise - leaving early is the most common deadly mistake
Agree as a family not to go out to pick up children or others - schools have their own shelter plans
Keep a battery or hand-crank radio with spare batteries (stored in a closed metal container) to hear official instructions
Decontamination plan: remove your outer clothing layer and bag it, then wash skin and hair with soap and water - do not scrub hard
Store at least 2 weeks of water in sealed containers before any event
Store at least 2 weeks of food in sealed cans or packages - wipe containers off before opening
Do not eat garden produce or drink from open outdoor sources until officials say they are safe
Keep N95 masks for each person to cover nose and mouth while moving to shelter
Know how to shut off fans, air conditioning, and forced-air heat and close fireplace dampers so outside air is not pulled in
Understand that fallout radiation drops fast in the first hours and days (the 7-10 rule of thumb: about 90% less for every 7-fold increase in time) - time inside is protection
Potassium iodide (KI) only protects the thyroid - take it only when officials tell you to, follow the package label, and never use iodine antiseptic or iodized salt instead
Keep long sleeves, gloves, and a hat to cover skin if you must go outside
Keep soap, shampoo, damp wipes, and plastic bags with ties in your shelter area for decontamination
Plan to bring pets inside and wash them with soap and water if they were outside
Learn your local emergency plan and how your area sends alerts (WEA, sirens, radio)
Write your out-of-area contact and meeting point on paper - text instead of calling to keep networks open
